KEY MESSAGE 1) 

Thunderstorm concerns.

1) Amidst diurnally-enhanced destabilization, some isolated/spotty 
storms are possible near/south of the OH Rvr by/past 21z as the 
subsidence influence from the midlevel ridge gradually shifts E of 
the region. Although there are uncertainties regarding coverage of 
convection, if there is to be development, the greatest coverage of 
late-day pulse convection will likely focus near/south of the OH Rvr 
within an extreme MLCAPE/DCAPE environment, but with little deep-
layer shear to sustain individual updrafts. This presents an 
environment that will be /very/ conducive to pulse convection and 
water-loaded downburst processes into a well-mixed BL, if storms are
able to initiate (lack of forcing/lift). The difficult aspect of 
this forecast is that the location, timing, and coverage of this 
storm potential for any one spot/area is quite uncertain, despite 
some of the ingredients being there for highly-localized, high-impact
storms. Aside from the lightning, which will be prolific with any 
activity that actually develops given the robust deep instby, strong 
to damaging downburst wind gusts are certainly in play as well. With 
very weak shear to support any sustained maintenance, alongside an 
extreme DCAPE in excess of 1200 J/kg into this evening, the downburst
potential will continue well past sunset until the BL slowly becomes
more stable by early overnight.

2) The second area to watch closely will be locations near/north of 
I-70 within a zone of slightly better forcing and deep-layer wind 
fields/shear, particularly after 00z. Several complexes of storms, 
initiating well upstream in parts of nrn IL/IN, will likely track E 
through the nrn OH Vly this evening into the early overnight. While 
the steering- layer flow is oriented more W-to-E, these more 
organized complexes may tend to pivot more to the SE with time toward
the better reservoir of instby located closer to the I-70 corridor, 
particularly after sunset. As such, there remains the distinct 
possibility that one or more linear complexes of storms drift SE into
nrn parts of the ILN FA late this evening into early tonight, 
bringing with them the potential for frequent lightning and 
strong/damaging wind gusts (as well as some isolated large hail). 
There is fairly low confidence regarding the timing/location of 
storms within this corridor, but there is enough of a signal (and 
therefore slightly higher confidence) within the near/short-term 
guidance to present this as a possibility from about 8 PM to 2 AM 
from EC IN into WC and central OH. The area of greatest concern is 
well-represented by the SPC SWODY1. Any activity through early 
tonight will also bring with it the potential for torrential 
downpours, with localized rainfall in excess of 1 inch in very short 
periods of times. Poor drainage areas may quickly be overwhelmed by 
brief intense rain rates. Those with outdoor plans this evening, 
particularly near/north of I-70 should monitor the weather closely 
and be prepared to take shelter should storms develop/move through 
your area.

KEY MESSAGE 2) 

Saturday will be another warm/very humid day, with temps likely to 
top out in the upper 80s to lower 90s with dewpoints making it feel 
like 100 degrees at times. That being said, fairly widespread 
convection by mid/late afternoon may bring an early end of the heat, 
with confidence increasing in fairly high coverage of storms by 
early evening area-wide. 

Although the convective forecast for later today brings with it some 
uncertainties, the setup for Saturday is even moreso, especially as 
it relates to timing/location for any one spot. This being said, 
what remains fairly certain as this juncture, is the expectation for 
greater coverage of storms on Saturday than will be the case today, 
particularly late afternoon into early evening. This will be in 
response to further suppression of the midlevel ridge and the 
corresponding diurnally-driven erosion of the cap. Additionally, in 
response to a weak system moving through the Great Lakes region, 
deep-layer wind fields should subtly increase into western parts of 
the region by Saturday evening, bringing a corresponding uptick in 
available shear for some low-end storm organization potential. 
Fairly widespread loosely-organized clusters of storms should 
develop as early as 2 PM Saturday, expanding in coverage into late 
afternoon and early evening as the outflows from localized 
downbursts set of a chain reaction of convective initiation across 
the OH Vly. The downburst/DCAPE environment locally on Saturday will 
again be quite ripe, meaning that any of the stronger storms will 
have the potential to produce localized strong to damaging wind 
gusts in the form of downbursts (as well as some isolated large 
hail).
